title: The golden lion, deeper
hookLine: Fazang's teaching: the gold and the lion's shape are one

lines: THE SHAPE IS GONE. THE GOLD ISN'T.
cards: A wedding ring. A family's old one, maybe, handed down. One day it's too small, so a jeweler melts it and makes it into something new: a pendant.
Is the ring gone? The shape is gone; nobody can wear it on a finger anymore. But not one grain of the gold has gone anywhere.

It's hanging around somebody's neck. Earlier on this path came Fazang's golden lion, the statue he used to teach an empress, and the basic idea: the gold, the lion's shape, not two. Today, a deeper look.

teach.b: In Fazang's essay, the lion doesn't make itself. It appears because a skilled worker shapes the gold. The lion depends on conditions, gold, a hand, a moment, so it has no lion-ness of its own.
That's emptiness, the same thing the Tiantai fist showed earlier this week. The gold doesn't change.

teach.h: MELTED OR MADE, THE GOLD IS THE SAME.
teach.b: When the lion is made, the gold gains nothing; when the lion is melted down, the gold loses nothing.
Fazang uses that to point at the deep nature of things, which isn't added to when a thing arises or taken away when it ends. Then, looking two ways.

teach.h: SEE THE LION, OR SEE THE GOLD.
teach.b: When you look at the lion, the essay says, there's only lion; the gold doesn't show. When you look at the gold, there's only gold; the lion doesn't show.
See both at once, and both are fully there, hidden and shown together. That is principle and event without obstruction, yesterday's teaching, made into a statue. And every part.
The lion's eye is gold, and so is its ear, and so is every hair.

teach.h: EACH HAIR HOLDS THE WHOLE LION.
teach.b: Because each part is gold through and through, Fazang says each part holds the whole lion. One hair, the whole beast.
Now look back across the week: Tiantai's three truths, Zhiyi's stopping and seeing, Huayan's garland, its lamps that don't crowd each other out, and this lion.
Two Chinese schools, two summits, and the same patient work: looking at an ordinary thing until the whole teaching shows through it.

how: Students of the Huayan tradition read Fazang's Essay on the Golden Lion as a short introduction to the school's teaching, contemplating the relation of the gold (principle) and the lion (event).

o: a statue Fazang gave the empress as a royal gift
a symbol of a king's power to rule over nature

games.q: you're looking at the golden lion. Fazang asks: when you see only the lion, where is the gold?
o: gone, until the lion is melted.
games.why: see the lion and the gold doesn't show; see the gold and the lion doesn't show. both are fully there, hidden and shown together.

practice: Choose something nearby, a wooden spoon, a clay bowl, a metal key, and name its form once, quietly: spoon.

Follow the material back, the wood a branch, and before that a tree drinking rain, then forward, to the day it cracks or burns and becomes something else. Then come back to the thing in your hand, here, now, wood shaped as a spoon.

wordCard.voice: The golden lion. Fazang's teaching image: the gold and the lion's shape are one, and each part of the lion holds the whole. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese Jin shizi zhang: the Essay on the Golden Lion, attributed to Fazang.

carryVoice: Your line: gold and lion. The shape comes and goes, and the gold stays just as it was. That closes the week.
